lines: ({player} knocks on the window. Melanie stands beside you wearing her most serious face.)
Ah. Melanie. And {player}. I know that face. This is about the slide again, isn't it.
{player}: Mr. Palmer, Galaxity needs a water slide.

lines.speaker: Melanie
lines.text: We don't even have a toy store!

lines: Melanie, I told you, you could have a toy store or a gaming store, and you chose the gaming store.
(Mr. Palmer points to the big map of Galaxity on his wall.)
Look at all this! A tree house. A zipline. A rock wall. An observatory. A cloud with a quiet side AND a loud side. A magic bubble bath.
This town has plenty of fun. The answer is no. Not now. Sometimes the best thing is to wait.
Patience, both of you. Patience.
(And the curtain swishes shut. You're sure you saw him wince when Melanie said "the old slide".)
({player} knocks. Melanie's beside you, holding a drawing of a cloud.)
Back again? You two are very patient. Hmm. That's rather the point, isn't it.
{player}: We went to the old slide. And the Haunted House. And something green and giggly got out.
Something got OUT? Oh dear. Oh dear oh dear. I'll... keep an eye on that. Nobody panic. Especially not Leo.

lines.speaker: Melanie
lines.text: But we have a new plan! It doesn't need the waterfall, or the Haunted House.

lines: (Melanie holds up the drawing: a fluffy cloud over the lake, a slide spiralling down into the water, and a little toy store sitting on top.)
...A floating cloud slide. Over the lake. With a toy store on top.
You waited. You listened. You found out why the old slide was closed, and you came back with something better.
That's what patience is for. Yes. YES! My builders will have it floating by your next visit.
(Mr. Palmer smiles, and closes the curtain very gently.)
({player} knocks, and holds up the Doggie Bill of Rights. Rex is beside you, standing very tall for a husky.)

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: Mr. Palmer! The Doggie Bill of Rights. Signed by the town. And one paw.

lines: Hm. Hm hm. "Rule one: dogs are welcome everywhere." "Rule two: the right to zoomies in the Market Square."
Rule one: yes. Dogs are welcome everywhere in Galaxity. I'll have a sign made, and a fountain at dog height.
Rule two: zoomies... in the mornings only. Before the flower stall opens. We had an incident with the tulips.
Well done, Rex. You listened to everybody, even Rook. That's what a good mayor does.

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: (whispering) Did you hear that? "A good mayor."

lines: ({player} knocks, and holds up the Doggie Bill of Rights. Rex is beside you, standing very tall for a husky.)

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: Mr. Palmer! The Doggie Bill of Rights. Signed by the town. And one paw.

lines: Hm. "Rule one: dogs are welcome everywhere." "Rule two: dogs may use the magic bubble bath."
Rule one: yes. Dogs are welcome everywhere in Galaxity. I'll have a sign made, and a fountain at dog height.
Rule two: yes, on Tuesdays. We'll need a LOT more bubbles. And a towel the size of a tent.
Well done, Rex. You listened to everybody, even Rook. That's what a good mayor does.

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: (whispering) Did you hear that? "A good mayor."

lines: ({player} knocks, and holds up the Doggie Bill of Rights. Rex is beside you, standing very tall for a husky.)

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: Mr. Palmer! The Doggie Bill of Rights. Signed by the town. And one paw.

lines: Hm. "Rule one: dogs are welcome everywhere." "Rule two: the right to sniff absolutely everything."
Rule one: yes. Dogs are welcome everywhere in Galaxity. I'll have a sign made, and a fountain at dog height.
Rule two: yes. But not my sandwiches. A mayor's sandwiches are private.
Well done, Rex. You listened to everybody, even Rook. That's what a good mayor does.

lines.speaker: Rex
lines.text: (whispering) Did you hear that? "A good mayor."

lines: Ah, {player}. Good. I was hoping you'd come through tonight.
The Agent of Chaos has been creeping closer, out in the far field. I'd like someone to have a look at him. From a nice, safe distance, mind.
And while you're out that way, there's an old iron gate in the northwest woods. The Scary World gate. Just peek. No need to go in.
Dash tells me the last two schematics are out there too. One in the Spooky Woods, and one in the far field, near... well. Near him.
Off you go. And {player}? Thank you. Galaxity is lucky to have you.
({player} knocks on the window. Tap, tap, tap.)
Coming, coming! Oh, hello, {player}! What can I do for you?
{player}: Mr. Palmer, I'm Rex's campaign manager. He wants to be mayor! Here are his ideas.
({player} tells him about the bike lane, the flowers, the lamps and the naps in the sun.)
Those are lovely ideas. Really lovely.
But I'm afraid the answer is no. Not this year. I'm still the mayor, and the next election isn't until next year.
{player}: Oh. Rex is going to be sad.
Tell him this from me: a good mayor is patient. And a good mayor listens to everybody before deciding anything.
And it sounds like he's already started. He asked the whole town! Even Rook!
Tell him to keep listening. And I'll put Bramble's flowers in the window boxes right away. Goodbye, {player}!
({player} knocks. Nobody answers. The curtains are closed.)
(A little sign on the window says: OFFICE HOURS: MORNING TILL TEATIME. Mr. Palmer)

rotate: Hello, {player}! Tell Future Mayor Rex the window flowers are coming along nicely.
Still listening to everybody? Good! Me too.

lines: ({player} knocks on the window. Tap, tap, tap.)
Hello there! I'm Mr. Palmer, the mayor of Galaxity. Lots of paperwork today!
{player}: Hi, Mr. Palmer! I'm {player}.
{player}! Welcome. My door is always open. Well... my window is.

rotate: Busy, busy! The town map needs updating again. Somebody moved the whole market!
Being mayor is mostly listening. And signing things. So many things.
(Mr. Palmer is on the phone.) Yes... yes... no, the portal is NOT a swimming pool. Goodbye!
